mainTopic: רבי טרפון's way for a ממזר to have non-ממזר children through a שפחה, and the opening of פרק עשרה יוחסין on the lineage groups that came up from בבל
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא about a master who frees his pregnant שפחה but says her child stays a slave. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the child goes free with her. The חכמים say the master's words stand, and רבא explains that the פסוק they quoted is really the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי. Next comes a משנה: רבי טרפון says a ממזר can have a child with a שפחה, and once that child is freed he is not a ממזר. רבי אליעזר says the child is a ממזר slave. The גמרא proves from the story of רבי שמלאי and his ממזר host that רבי טרפון allows this לכתחילה, and שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי טרפון. The גמרא then debates the word 'לו', which רבי אליעזר uses as his source, and the רבנן answer that a שפחה's child is like an animal's young and takes no lineage from the father. The פרק 'האומר' ends, and the new פרק 'עשרה יוחסין' lists ten lineage groups that came up from בבל and who may marry whom. The גמרא explains that 'went up' teaches that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands, and it begins checking the sources for this on the next amud.

steps.title: Freeing a maidservant but not her child
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a master frees his pregnant שפחה but says her child stays a slave. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the child goes free like her. The חכמים say the master's words stand, and they quote a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a master tells his maidservant, 'You are free, but your child is a slave,' רבי יוסי הגלילי says the child is free like her. The חכמים say it works the way the master said, because the פסוק says, 'The wife and her children shall be her master's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with a disagreement: can a master free a pregnant שפחה while keeping her unborn child as a slave?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that the unborn child is treated like part of the mother, so freeing her frees the child too. The חכמים hold that the master can split them, so the mother is free and the child stays a slave. The חכמים attach a פסוק to their view, and the next step questions that.

keyTerms.meaning: His words stand, meaning what he said takes effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the child is FREE like the mother. The חכמים say the child STAYS a slave as the master declared.

phrases.english: One who says to his maidservant:
phrases.notes: She is pregnant; the 'child' is still unborn.

phrases.english: "You are hereby a free woman,
but your offspring is a slave" –
the offspring is like her,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
And the Sages say: his words stand,
because it is said:
"The wife and her children shall be her master's."

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the unborn child goes free with the mother. חכמים: the master's split declaration works, so the child stays a slave.

steps.title: How does the verse prove the Sages' view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the derivation from the פסוק is, since it does not seem to support the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the learning here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised. It asks how the פסוק quoted for the חכמים proves their opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the children belong with the mother, so it seems to point the other way, toward 'the child follows the mother.' That is the opposite of what the חכמים say. So the question is really a challenge to the way the פסוק was used.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the derivation? How is this learned?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof-verse attached to the חכמים in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק cited as the source for the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says the children go with the mother, which supports the child following her status, not the master splitting them.

steps.title: רבא: the verse belongs to רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the פסוק is not the source for the חכמים. It is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it goes on רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the question by moving the פסוק to the other side. It is the reason for רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the פסוק teaches that children follow their mother, so when she goes free the child goes free too. That is exactly רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. The חכמים simply rely on the master's words taking effect.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא (a sage of the גמרא period)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'the wife and her children shall be her master's' supports רבי יוסי הגלילי: the child follows the mother. It is not the source for the חכמים.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It refers to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק is the reason for רבי יוסי הגלילי's view, not for the חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the proof-verse to the other opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק was the source for the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי: children follow the mother's status.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: a ממזר's line can become pure
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי טרפון says a ממזר can have children who are not ממזרים: he has a child with a שפחה, the child is a slave, and once freed the child is a regular free man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: ממזרים can become pure. How? If a ממזר marries a שפחה, the child is a slave. If the child is then freed, the son turns out to be a free man.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי טרפון describes a way for a ממזר to have descendants who are not ממזרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child born to a שפחה takes the mother's status, so he is a slave and not a ממזר. When that slave is freed, he becomes a free man with no ממזר status. In this way the ממזר status stops with the father.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born of a forbidden union, who may not marry a regular Jew
To be purified, meaning to have descendants free of ממזר status

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Tarfon says:
Mamzerim can be purified.
phrases.notes: 'Purified' here means their children can be free of ממזר status. It has nothing to do with טומאה.

phrases.english: How so?
A mamzer who married a maidservant,
the child is a slave;
if he freed him,
phrases.notes: The master of the slave child frees him.

phrases.english: the son is found to be a free man.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: יְכוֹלִין מַמְזֵרִין לִיטָּהֵר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son of a ממזר and a שפחה is a slave, not a ממזר. Once freed, he is a regular free man.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the child is a ממזר slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי טרפון. The child is a slave who is also a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: this child is a ממזר slave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the opposing view in the משנה and rejects רבי טרפון's method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the child carries the father's ממזר status even while he is a slave. So freeing him does not help, because he would still be a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave who also has ממזר status

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון: a ממזר plus a שפחה produces a slave who can be freed and become a regular free man. רבי אליעזר: the child stays a ממזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
This is a mamzer slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי זֶה עֶבֶד מַמְזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי טרפון in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child of a ממזר and a שפחה is a ממזר slave, so the method does not work.

steps.title: Does רבי טרפון allow this from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי טרפון permits a ממזר to marry a שפחה from the start (לכתחילה), or only says the result works after it has happened (דיעבד).
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: is רבי טרפון saying this לכתחילה, or is he saying it דיעבד?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a question about how far רבי טרפון's ruling goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון clearly holds that the freed son is not a ממזר. What is unclear is whether a ממזר may go ahead and marry a שפחה for this purpose, or whether the ruling only describes the result once it has already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the Sages)
From the outset, allowed to do it in the first place
After the fact, valid only once already done

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree רבי טרפון holds the freed son is not a ממזר. The question is only whether the ממזר may plan this from the start.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A dilemma was raised before them:
Did Rabbi Tarfon state it ab initio,
or did he state it after the fact?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי טרפון permits a ממזר to marry a שפחה לכתחילה, or only validates the result דיעבד.

steps.title: Proof: you purified the males but not the females
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a proof from a ברייתא. The Sages told רבי טרפון that his method purifies male ממזרים but not female ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: they said to רבי טרפון, 'You have purified the males, but you have not purified the females.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a source to answer the question about לכתחילה or דיעבד. This step sets up the proof, and Step 8 explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages point out a limit of רבי טרפון's method: it works for a male ממזר but not for a female one. The way they phrase it as a complaint is what the גמרא will use to decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, an introduction to a proof

phrases.english: Come and hear:
They said to Rabbi Tarfon:
You have purified the males,
but you have not purified the females.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 6 from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי טרפון's method is meant לכתחילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which the Sages tell רבי טרפון that he purified the males but not the females

steps.title: Finishing the proof: if it were allowed from the start, a ממזרת could marry a slave too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the proof from the ברייתא. If רבי טרפון allowed his method לכתחילה, why couldn't a ממזרת also marry a slave and have slave children?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say רבי טרפון meant it as something you may plan from the start, then a ממזרת should also be allowed to marry a slave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא from Step 7 seems to prove that רבי טרפון only meant דיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said רבי טרפון's method helps males but not females. If the method were a planned, allowed fix, the same trick should work for a ממזרת by marrying a slave. Since the ברייתא says it does not work for females, it looks like רבי טרפון only meant the result is valid after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as a plan you are allowed to carry out
After the fact; the result counts once it has already happened

phrases.english: And if you say he said it as allowed from the start,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי טרפון, from the question in Step 6.

phrases.english: then a ממזרת should also marry a slave!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the logic of the proof begun in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי טרפון only meant דיעבד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where the חכמים said his method purifies males but not females.

steps.title: A slave has no family line, so the trick cannot help a ממזרת
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. A child of a slave father follows the mother, so a ממזרת's child would still be a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave has no family lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 8 by giving a different reason why the method fails for women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child of a slave is not counted as his child, so the child follows the Jewish mother and is a ממזר. That is why the method cannot work for a ממזרת, even if it were allowed לכתחילה. So the ברייתא proves nothing about לכתחילה or דיעבד.

phrases.english: A slave has no family lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The method fails for females because a slave's child follows the mother, not because the method is only דיעבד.

steps.title: Proof from רבי שמלאי and his ממזר host
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי told his ממזר host that if he had met him earlier, he would have purified his sons. That fits only if the method may be planned לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמלאי's host was a ממזר, and רבי שמלאי told him, 'If I had come to you earlier, I would have purified your sons.' This makes sense if the method is allowed from the start. But if it only works after the fact, what advice could he have given?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, a story about רבי שמלאי, to show that רבי טרפון meant לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving advice ahead of time means telling someone to do this on purpose. If the method is allowed לכתחילה, the advice was simply 'marry a שפחה.' If it only works דיעבד, it is unclear what advice רבי שמלאי could have given at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; the גמרא brings a proof
His host, the man he stayed with
I would have purified them, made them not ממזרים

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Simlai's host
was a mamzer, and he said to him:
If I had come to you earlier,
I would have purified your sons.
Granted, if you say it is allowed from the start, that is fine,
but if you say it only works after the fact,
what would it be?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what advice could רבי שמלאי have given him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי שמלאי and his ממזר host.

steps.title: Maybe the advice was: become a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי שמלאי's advice might have been to steal and be sold as an עבד עברי. Then he could be with a שפחה without planning a marriage to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would have advised him: go steal, and get sold as a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to push off the proof by finding advice that works even if רבי טרפון only meant דיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד עברי may be given a שפחה כנענית by his master. So the ממזר could have slave children through that route instead of deliberately marrying a שפחה. That would explain רבי שמלאי's words without proving לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish (Hebrew) slave, for example a thief sold to pay back what he stole

phrases.english: That he would give him advice and say to him:
Go steal, and be sold as a Hebrew slave.
phrases.notes: An עבד עברי is allowed to be with a שפחה כנענית, so his children would be slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'what would the advice be?' from Step 10, to push off the proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The advice could have been to become an עבד עברי, so it need not show that marrying a שפחה is allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: There was no Hebrew slave in רבי שמלאי's time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the suggestion. An עבד עברי only exists when יובל is kept, and it was not kept in רבי שמלאי's days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in רבי שמלאי's years, was there such a thing as an עבד עברי? Didn't the Master teach that עבד עברי only applies when יובל applies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the advice suggested in Step 11 was impossible in רבי שמלאי's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that עבד עברי is tied to יובל. In רבי שמלאי's era יובל was no longer kept, so nobody could be sold as an עבד עברי. That means this cannot have been his advice.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say? It brings a known teaching to challenge

phrases.english: But in the years of Rabbi Simlai,
was there a Hebrew slave?
But didn't the Master say:
A Hebrew slave does not apply
except at a time when the Jubilee applies!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִשְׁנֵי דְּרַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי עֶבֶד עִבְרִי מִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the suggestion in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי שמלאי advised becoming an עבד עברי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עבד עברי only exists when יובל is kept, and it was not kept in רבי שמלאי's time.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי טרפון meant from the start
steps.stepSummary: Since there is no other possible advice, the גמרא concludes that רבי טרפון allows a ממזר to marry a שפחה לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So must we not learn from this that רבי טרפון meant it as allowed from the start? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question from Step 6 with a firm answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only advice רבי שמלאי could have meant was 'marry a שפחה.' So רבי טרפון's method is something a ממזר may plan on purpose, not just a result that counts after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the proof stands

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון allows a ממזר to marry a שפחה כנענית לכתחילה, so his children are slaves who can be freed as non-ממזרים.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this
that Rabbi Tarfon said it as allowed from the start?
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the pushback in Step 11 knocked down, the proof from Step 10 stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי טרפון's method is allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל, rules that the הלכה is like רבי טרפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling on the מחלוקת between רבי טרפון and רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together with Step 13, this means a ממזר may, in practice, marry a שפחה לכתחילה to have children who can become free and not ממזרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a real, allowed path for a ממזר to have descendants who are not ממזרים.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final practical ruling after the conclusion in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is like רבי טרפון.

steps.title: The source for רבי אליעזר: the word 'his' in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי אליעזר's view from the משנה. רבי אלעזר explains it from the word 'לו' in the פסוק about ממזר: the child follows the parent with the flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: this child is a slave who is also a ממזר. רבי אלעזר said: what is רבי אליעזר's reason? The פסוק says 'his,' which teaches: follow his flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's line from the משנה again in order to find the source for his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the child of a שפחה is a slave and nothing more. רבי אליעזר learns from the word 'לו' that the ממזר father's flaw also passes down. So the child is both a slave and a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave who is also a ממזר
His flaw, the parent with the defective status

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names: רבי אֱלִיעֶזֶר is the תנא in the משנה, and רבי אֶלְעָזָר is a later Sage explaining his reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
This is a slave who is a mamzer.
Rabbi Elazar said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
As the verse says: "his"
follow the one with his flaw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with רבי טרפון, the גמרא turns to the other side of the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר learns from 'לו' that the child follows the ממזר father's flaw, so he is a slave and a ממזר.

steps.title: How the Rabbis use the word 'לו'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the word 'לו' is needed for a different case: a regular Jew who married a ממזרת. Without it, we might think the child follows the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do the רבנן read 'לו'? It is about a regular Jew who married a ממזרת. You might have thought the child follows the father, because it says 'by their families, by their fathers' houses.' So 'לו' comes to take him out of that rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן explain the word 'לו', since they do not learn רבי אליעזר's rule from it. They answer that it teaches about a Jew married to a ממזרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that lineage follows the father ('לבית אבותם'). If a regular Jew married a ממזרת, that rule would make the child a regular Jew. 'לו' teaches that here the child follows the flawed parent and is a ממזר, but the רבנן say it says nothing about a שפחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis. Here it means רבי טרפון's side of the debate.
You might have thought (a mistaken first idea)
By their fathers' houses. Lineage follows the father.
Took him out (excluded him from the rule)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That verse is about a Jew who married a ממזרת.
phrases.notes: The 'Rabbis' here are רבי טרפון's side. The question is what they do with the word 'לו' from step 15.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
'By their families, by their fathers' houses' is written,
so 'of his' came and took him out.
phrases.notes: In other words, the child does not follow the father here. He follows the ממזרת mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's own use of the word that רבי אליעזר used as his source in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the רבנן learn from 'לו' if they reject רבי אליעזר's rule?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לו' teaches that the child of a Jew and a ממזרת is a ממזר, even though lineage normally follows the father.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: 'לו' overrides the שפחה verse too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues that if 'לו' can override 'לבית אבותם', it can also override the verse 'the woman and her children belong to her master.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? Even though it says 'by their fathers' houses', 'לו' came and took him out. Here too, even though it says 'the woman and her children shall be her master's', 'לו' comes and takes him out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the רבנן using their own example. Just as 'לו' beats the general father rule, it should also beat the general rule for a שפחה's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that 'לו' can override a clear verse ('לבית אבותם'). So רבי אליעזר says it should also override 'האשה וילדיה תהיה לאדוניה'. That would make a ממזר's child from a שפחה a ממזר too, following the flawed parent.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman and her children shall be her master's. A שפחה's child is a slave like her.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתַב
phrases.english: And רבי אליעזר? Is it not so that even though it is written
'By their families, by their fathers' houses,'
'of his' came and took him out?

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתִיב
phrases.english: Here too, even though it is written
'The woman and her children shall be her master's,'
'of his' comes and takes him out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the רבנן's own example from step 16 into support for רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that the child of a ממזר and a שפחה is a ממזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן's admission that 'לו' overrides 'לבית אבותם'
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's claim in step 16 that 'לו' only teaches about a Jew who married a ממזרת and does not apply to a שפחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן admit that 'לו' overrides the clear verse 'לבית אבותם'. So it should also override 'האשה וילדיה תהיה לאדוניה' and make the child follow the flawed ממזר father.

steps.title: A שפחה's child is like an animal's young
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reply that the two cases are different. A שפחה's unborn child is like an animal's unborn young, so it has no connection to the father's lineage at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Any child in the womb of a כנענית שפחה is considered like the young in the womb of an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן explain why 'לו' cannot override the שפחה verse. The child of a שפחה never takes on the father's lineage at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a ממזרת, both parents are Jewish, so 'לו' only decides which parent the child follows. A כנענית שפחה's child is legally like an animal's young: it has no Jewish lineage from the father. So the child is a slave like the mother, and the father's flaw does not pass on.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן (רבי טרפון) hold that a שפחה's child takes only the mother's status. That is why a ממזר's child from a שפחה can be freed and become a full Jew.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? Any child in the womb

phrases.aramaic: שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית כְּוָלָד בִּמְעֵי בְּהֵמָה דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: of a Canaanite maidservant is considered like the young in the womb of an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: כׇּל וָלָד בִּמְעֵי שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's comparison by showing the שפחה case is a different kind of case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If 'לו' overrides 'לבית אבותם', it should also override 'האשה וילדיה תהיה לאדוניה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שפחה's child has no lineage from the father at all, so 'לו' does not apply to that case.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter 'האומר'
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the third פרק of קידושין, 'האומר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'האומר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פרק 'האומר' with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
'The one who says.' The name of the third פרק of קידושין.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'The One Who Says'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final debate ends.

steps.title: Ten lineage groups came up from Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה (פרק 'עשרה יוחסין') lists ten groups of lineage among the Jews who came up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten lineage groups came up from בבל: כהנים, לויים, ישראלים, חללים, converts, freed slaves, ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקים and אסופים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins. The משנה lists ten groups of Jewish lineage that came up from בבל, setting up the discussion of who may marry whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves from the most respected lineage (כהנים) to people whose lineage is flawed or unknown (שתוקי, אסופי). The rest of the פרק explains the marriage rules between these groups.

keyTerms.meaning: חללים, children of a כהן born from a marriage forbidden to a כהן. They lose כהונה.
נתינים, descendants of the גבעונים who converted in the days of יהושע
שתוקים, people who know their mother but not their father
אסופים, foundlings who know neither parent

steps.confusionAlert: שתוקי and אסופי are not proven ממזרים. Their lineage is simply unknown, so they are treated as a doubt.

phrases.english: Ten lineage groups came up from Babylonia:
Priests, Levites, Israelites,
disqualified priests, converts, and freed slaves,
mamzerim, Gibeonites, those of unknown father, and foundlings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new chapter after the Hadran.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten lineage groups came up from בבל: כהני, לויי, ישראלי, חללי, גירי, חרורי, ממזירי, נתיני, שתוקי, אסופי.

steps.title: The first two circles of who may marry whom
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that כהנים, לוים and ישראלים may marry each other. It then rules that לוים, ישראלים, חללים, גרים and freed slaves may marry each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Priests, Levites and Israelites are allowed to marry one another. Levites, Israelites, חללים, converts and freed slaves are allowed to marry one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts explaining the ten groups it just listed. It tells us which groups are allowed to marry each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first circle covers the three families of pure lineage. The second circle drops the כהנים, because a כהן may not marry a חללה or a גיורת. It adds חללים, גרים and freed slaves, who may marry ישראלים and לוים.

keyTerms.meaning: חללים: children of a כהן from a marriage forbidden to him; they lose כהונה

steps.confusionAlert: לויים and ישראלים appear in both lists. That is because they may marry the first group (כהנים) and also the second group (חללים, גרים, freed slaves).

phrases.english: Priests, Levites, and Israelites
are permitted to marry one another.
Levites, Israelites, חללים, converts, and freed slaves
are permitted to marry one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּהֲנֵי לְוִיֵּי וְיִשְׂרְאֵלֵי מוּתָּרִין לָבֹא זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the marriage rules for the ten groups listed in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים may intermarry. לוים, ישראלים, חללים, גרים and freed slaves may intermarry.

steps.title: The third circle of who may marry whom
steps.stepSummary: Converts, freed slaves, ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקי and אסופי may all marry one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Converts, freed slaves, ממזרים, Gibeonites, people whose father is unknown, and foundlings are all allowed to marry one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third circle. These groups may all marry each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גרים and freed slaves appear again. They may marry ישראלים, and they may also marry the groups of flawed or doubtful lineage, such as ממזרים. Everyone else in this list may not marry a regular ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: ממזרים: children of a forbidden union
שתוקי: someone whose father is unknown
אסופי: a foundling whose parents are both unknown

phrases.english: Converts, freed slaves, ממזרים, and Gibeonites
people of unknown father, and foundlings
all of them are permitted to marry one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּירֵי וַחֲרוֹרֵי מַמְזֵירֵי וּנְתִינֵי שְׁתוּקֵי וַאֲסוּפֵי כּוּלָּם מוּתָּרִין לָבֹא זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the third and last marriage circle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גרים, freed slaves, ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקי and אסופי may all marry one another.

steps.title: Defining שתוקי and אסופי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines a שתוקי as someone who knows his mother but not his father. It defines an אסופי as someone found in the street who knows neither parent. אבא שאול called a שתוקי a 'בדוקי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the definitions: a שתוקי is anyone who knows who his mother is but not who his father is. An אסופי is anyone picked up from the street who knows neither his father nor his mother. אבא שאול used to call a שתוקי a 'בדוקי'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what the last two groups mean. It also records another name that אבא שאול used for a שתוקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both groups are people whose lineage is in doubt. They might be ממזרים, so they are placed in the third circle. אבא שאול's different name for the שתוקי hints that he sees this person differently; the משנה does not explain why here.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא quoted in the משנה
'Checked one', אבא שאול's name for a שתוקי

steps.whatToRemember: The ten groups are sorted into three circles of who may marry whom. The last two groups, שתוקי and אסופי, are people whose lineage is unknown.

phrases.english: And these are they:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתוּקִי כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר אֶת אִמּוֹ
phrases.english: A שתוקי is anyone who knows his mother
but does not know his father.
An אסופי is anyone who was picked up from the marketplace

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מַכִּיר לֹא אֶת אָבִיו וְלֹא אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: and knows neither his father nor his mother.
אבא שאול would call a שתוקי a 'בדוקי'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵם שְׁתוּקִי כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר אֶת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines two of the groups named in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שתוקי knows his mother but not his father. An אסופי knows neither parent.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'went up from בבל'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's opening line and asks why it says the families 'went up from בבל' rather than simply 'went to ארץ ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Ten lineage groups went up from בבל.' Why does it specifically say 'went up from בבל'? It could have said 'they went to ארץ ישראל'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It looks closely at the exact wording of the משנה's first line and asks why that wording was chosen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the משנה is about family lineage, so the starting place and the word 'went up' seem unnecessary. The גמרא assumes every word of a משנה is chosen carefully. It wants to know what extra lesson this wording teaches.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Ten lineage groups went up from Babylonia.
Why does it specifically teach 'went up from Babylonia'?
Let it teach 'they went to ארץ ישראל'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא's first question about the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה chose the words 'went up from בבל' instead of 'went to ארץ ישראל'.

steps.title: The wording teaches that ארץ ישראל is higher than other lands
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches a side lesson. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that the בית המקדש is higher than all of ארץ ישראל, and that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is teaching us something in passing, as a ברייתא says. The פסוק says 'And you shall arise and go up to the place that ה׳ your God will choose.' This teaches that the בית המקדש is higher than all of ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'went up' teaches an extra idea along the way: ארץ ישראל is higher than all other countries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because ארץ ישראל is higher, travel there from בבל is called 'going up.' The ברייתא backs this with a פסוק that speaks of 'going up' to the בית המקדש. The ברייתא adds a second level as well: the מקדש is higher than the rest of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter in passing (a side lesson)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method: a word in a משנה that seems extra is explained as carrying a hidden lesson.

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: It teaches us a matter in passing,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
'And you shall arise and go up'

phrases.aramaic: אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״,
phrases.english: 'to the place that the Lord your God shall choose,'

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ גָּבוֹהַּ מִכׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: this teaches that the Temple is higher than all of ארץ ישראל,
and ארץ ישראל is higher than all the lands.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Went up' teaches that ארץ ישראל is higher than all lands, as a ברייתא learns from a פסוק. The same ברייתא says the מקדש is higher than all of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Granted the מקדש is higher, since a פסוק says so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the בית המקדש being higher than ארץ ישראל has a source in a פסוק. It is setting up a question about where the second claim comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the בית המקדש is higher than all of ארץ ישראל, because that is what is written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It grants the first half of the ברייתא and is about to quote the פסוק for it, before asking about the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בשלמא' means 'it makes sense for this part.' It usually leads to a challenge on another part, here the claim that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands. The quote and the challenge continue past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (leads into a challenge on another part)

phrases.english: Granted, the Temple
is higher than all of ארץ ישראל;
that is what is written:

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ גָּבוֹהַּ מִכׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins checking the sources for the two claims of the ברייתא in step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where in a פסוק each claim of the ברייתא is found. The first claim is granted here; the source for the second claim is about to be questioned.
